- Main integration topics: SDK setup, auth & key management, routing/model variants, and auditing.

Action items we agreed:
1) Technical deep-dive focused on authentication patterns & key rotation (Dev to lead).
2) Marissa to send collateral: SDK auth patterns + mutual action plan (attached).
3) FintechCo to confirm current KMS/Vault setup and preferred token model (API keys vs short-lived tokens).

Notes/Recommendations (summary):
- Short-lived JWTs minted by your auth service + service accounts for machine-to-machine is our recommended path for production (good for rotation and least-privilege).
- Keep API keys for legacy or internal-only tooling; restrict scope and rotate regularly.
- Integrate signing key management with your KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) and expose a JWKS endpoint for verifier rotation.
- Use scoped tokens for sensitive ops (e.g., embeddings:write, rerank:read).
- Consider per-environment prefixes and a token TTL of ~15m for high-risk APIs; refresh via a short-lived client credential flow.

Attachments: Redwood-SDK-Auth-Patterns.pdf, MVP-MAP.xlsx (attached).

Thanks Priya — great questions. Dropping some implementation details and links + a couple of attachments that should help.

Summary recommendations (concrete):
- Service accounts + short-lived JWTs: Mint short-lived JWTs from your internal auth service. Sign with a KMS-managed asymmetric key. Publish the public key via a JWKS endpoint that we use to verify at the Redwood edge. Rotation is handled by adding a new key to KMS and updating JWKS; we verify both new and recent previous keys for a configurable grace window.

- Rotation playbook (high level):
  1) Create new signing key in KMS (asymmetric).
  2) Publish new key in JWKS and mark as active in your auth service.
  3) Redwood accepts tokens signed by both active and previous-key (grace window configurable, default 24h).
  4) After grace window, revoke old key in KMS.

- Token model & scopes:
  - Access tokens: TTL ~15m for high-risk ops; 1h for lower-risk (configurable).
  - Refresh flow: client credentials grant to mint fresh access tokens; no long-lived bearer keys in clients.
  - Scopes example: embeddings:write, embeddings:read, rerank:read, rerank:write, admin:models.

- Legacy/API keys: supported for non-production/CI flows. We recommend per-env prefixes (prod-, staging-) and enforced rotation every 90 days. You can bind API keys to IP ranges.

- Auditing: Include per-request metadata (caller service, service-account-id, request-id). Redwood Console surfaces token-level latency and cost breakdowns; we can also stream audit logs to your SIEM (S3/Kinesis/CloudWatch).

Attachments: short-lived-jwt-sample.txt (example JWT minting flow and curl), key-rotation-playbook.pdf (detailed steps + rollback). Also see: https://docs.redwood.ai/auth/jwt for the public guide.

Code snippet (minting flow, pseudo):
  1) Client authenticates to internal auth service (mTLS or SAML/OIDC).
  2) Auth service calls KMS to sign JWT payload with key-id K1.
  3) Auth service returns signed JWT (TTL 15m).
  4) Client calls Redwood with Authorization: Bearer <jwt>.

If you want, we can run through a short network diagram during the deep-dive to map where keys live and who has access. I can also share a sample Vault + KMS integration we use for another customer.

Proposed slots: Tue 5/5 10:00 PT — confirmed by Priya; I’ll join. Alternative Wed 5/6 11:00 PT if needed.
